source.title: Loss Function Dynamics and Landscape for Deep Neural Networks Trained with Quadratic Loss
source.authors: M. Nakhodnov; M. Kodryan; E. Lobacheva; D. Vetrov

record.file_problem: Full text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Trains randomly initialized CIFAR10 ConvNets with SGD and reports training classification error across learning rates and loss functions.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports curvature, test error, and mode connectivity, but these do not themselves measure the claim versions. Cited results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study measures CIFAR-10 training classification error in a new setting: batch-normalized ConvNets with fixed output parameters and sphere-constrained SGD. These results test V1. Learning-rate phases alone do not test V5 because no stability threshold is established.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors identify three learning-rate-dependent phases in sphere-constrained scale-invariant networks for both losses, and report related behavior in unconstrained VGG16BN experiments. They interpret their results as supporting the hypothesis that MSE needs more iterations or parameters than cross-entropy for comparable convergence; they do not establish that requirement through a controlled width comparison.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SGD from a shared random initialization on a four-layer batch-normalized ConvNet with CIFAR10, but fixes affine batch-normalization parameters and the last linear layer, normalizes weights onto a unit sphere, and studies effective learning rates. Also tests MSE, no augmentation, and no momentum or L2 regularization in its baseline setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Training outcomes vary with effective learning rate and loss function; MSE on the full training set does not reach zero error in 6000 iterations.

fits_no_version.finding: Learning-rate-dependent convergence, chaotic equilibrium, and random-walk phases are characterized using curvature and trajectory correlations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sphere-constrained training exhibits distinct dynamical phases as the effective learning rate changes.

record.problems: The main setup fixes batch-normalization affine parameters and the last linear layer, uses CIFAR10 without augmentation, and evaluates one four-layer architecture. Many learning-rate-specific outcomes appear only in figures, and no uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional training-error results with explicit text descriptions were identified. Figures 18 and 20 show MSE results, including the CIFAR10 10% subset, but the text does not state whether that subset reaches zero training error.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, and controlled comparisons of model size or early stopping. Appendix 4 includes weight decay, but does not establish the substantial training-error outcome named for some regularized recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-minimum frequencies, and extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent degradation and comparisons with identity shortcuts.
Comparisons of initialization schemes for training speed or trainable depth.
Recovery above a measured initial stability threshold, full-batch edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence from below that threshold.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: Training-error outcomes for unconverged first-phase cross-entropy models and second-phase models. The text reports poorer fitting at small learning rates and a sharp loss of zero-error convergence at the second-phase boundary; numerical errors are needed to distinguish near-zero fitting from substantial error.

VGG16BN training outcomes with freely trained affine and output parameters, without sphere projection, for weight decay 0 and 10−4. The text reports first-phase subgroups and high-learning-rate NaN divergence without weight decay; classification-error values require inspection of the figures.
Actual full-dataset MSE training-error values after 6000 iterations, needed to determine whether R3 nevertheless reaches near-zero error.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains figure captions but no readable plotted values. Failure to reach exactly zero error therefore cannot automatically be treated as failure to reach near-zero error. The MSE subset experiments are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes are not tested.
